fields.description:
The LLM completion verifier is budget-impractical for code-heavy, multi-criteria tickets.

## Context
Discovered dogfooding the close gate on this feature's own epic + workstreams. On a faster, decisive model (sonnet) a FOCUSED ticket (≈2 small AC) converges in ~12s, but a code-heavy workstream whose AC reference large files (e.g. WS-3: ~4 AC across `_cli/__init__.py` ~1000 lines, `mcp_server.py`, test files) does NOT converge even at recursion_limit=500 / ~560s. The agent reads many large files / searches across criteria; there is no cheap shortcut to verifying implementation-completeness of a code-heavy ticket. With the gate enabled, such tickets currently can't be closed without a very high REBAR_LLM_MAX_STEPS or `--force-close`.

## Candidate directions
- A lightweight repo-map / orientation (tree-sitter/PageRank à la Aider) so the agent reads less.
- Stronger budget steering (hard tool-call cap) and/or summarized-file reads.
- The framework-wide AutoStrategy/ProviderStrategy migration (separate follow-up) for cheaper structured output.
- Per-ticket file-impact hints (`set_file_impact`) to focus the agent on the relevant files.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] A code-heavy multi-criteria workstream ticket verifies (PASS/FAIL) within a practical
      budget/latency on the default verifier model. MET: the ToolStrategy root-cause fix (ticket
      `c7c5`) moved WS-3 from a timeout at recursion_limit=500 (~560s) to a **78s PASS** via
      `output_strategy='extract'`. `sonnet` is the decisive default; `opus` over-explores.
- [x] A decision is recorded on how to make the gate practical for code-heavy tickets.
      REMEDIATED 2026-08-07 — the original wording offered three options (raise the default budget,
      add a repo-map, scope the gate to focused tickets) and the actual answer was NONE of them: the
      convergence failure was root-caused and fixed outright, so no budget was raised, no repo-map was
      built, and the gate's scope was not narrowed. The criterion is rewritten to state what was
      genuinely decided rather than force-closing past an option list that reality overtook.

## Follow-on work — owned elsewhere

Three OPTIONAL optimizations surfaced by the prior-art research are explicitly NOT part of this
ticket and are owned by another session under a separate ticket:
* per-criterion fan-out (LangGraph Send + a deterministic reducer),
* per-criterion context PRE-SELECTION (Aider repo-map / FastContext line-ranges) so the agent does not
  hunt through large files,
* small bounded per-unit budgets.

None of them blocks anything: the practical-budget problem this ticket was filed for is solved.
